issues.reason: Core patterns' "assert only what the text states" is violated: "undesired" restricts the object of the purpose clause, and (Inheritance suitor undesired) (STV 0.9 0.9) asserts the empirical generic that suitors in general are undesired, which the words never put there.

Recipient is defined as "goal of a transfer (indirect object / 'to'), including the addressee of communication", and a passive "carries exactly the roles its active would" — PeopleSoft is equip's direct object, so it takes a direct-object role, not Recipient.

Thematic roles states "a prepositional verb's object is this oblique, never a direct-object role ... the direct-object roles are for objects the verb takes WITHOUT a preposition" (its own example "dealt with the appeal"), so the object of "equipped with" cannot sit in Theme.

The reviewer's own gap records that a "known as <term-of-art>" label has no licensed carrier (Name takes proper nouns only), and (Member sk_defence_1 poison_pill) is true — a defence known as a poison pill IS a poison pill, unlike the opinion reports "considered / said to be" that the instruction set bars from flattening — so this is acceptable improvisation in gap territory.

gaps_confirmed: a "known as <quoted term>" nickname appositive: Name carries a string literal for proper nouns only, and the reduced-relative reading would force an odd know event
a restrictive adjective on a bare / generic plural object ("thwart undesired suitors"): a bare class symbol admits no modifier, and Inheritance on the kind asserts a generic the text does not state
new_gaps: a reduced-relative participial post-modifier ("designed to ...", "known as ...") is given the ordinary event form, but whether it carries its own tense atom ("which WAS designed") is unstated — the parse emits none
"equip X with Y": whether the equipped entity counts as physically/state-changed (Patient) or as an unchanged holder (Theme) is not settled by the change test as written
repair_summary: Removed the unlicensed generic (Inheritance suitor undesired) — no licensed carrier exists for the restrictive adjective on a bare plural object, so the false atom is dropped rather than replaced; changed (Recipient sk_equip_1 peoplesoft) to (Patient sk_equip_1 peoplesoft), the direct-object role the active would give (equipping changes the object's state); changed (Theme sk_equip_1 sk_defence_1) to the preposition-named oblique (With sk_equip_1 sk_defence_1) per the prepositional-verb rule; proof ids for the two changed atoms renamed to match their new heads.
notes: Patient rather than Theme for PeopleSoft follows the "applying a treatment changes the object" branch (fitting a defence to a company alters it), and a state change need not be physical. Nothing else was touched.
